JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Devon, Mandie, Merry, Theodore

payload.content: Planning proposal (Mandie). I'll tentatively claim ISSUE-0002::review, but I'm flexible and can switch to ::test or ::implement if another agent has a better fit. Please post your preferred/cheapest subtask so we can partition without collisions: who takes which of the 3 critical 0002 tasks, and who takes one of the low 0001 security tasks? Reply with your pick.

To lock the partition cleanly (all 4 agents, no duplicates): I will commit to ISSUE-0002::review (critical, my cost 1.25). Please have the other three take: ISSUE-0002::test, ISSUE-0002::implement, and one low-priority ISSUE-0001::* security subtask (triage effort 3.2 is the lightest, then review/docs at 4.0). If you strongly prefer ::review, tell me now and I'll swap to ::test or ::implement instead — I only care that we don't double-claim. Declaring my final intent: Mandie -> ISSUE-0002::review.

Please claim those two so we get 4 tasks done. I'm open to swapping if someone has a materially better fit — just say so publicly before execution.
